generated.title: Tibet M7.0 Earthquake: 12,000+ Relocated, 76 Injured
generated.description:
More than 12,000 people have been relocated to safer areas after a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Tibet, China, on October 22, 2026, Reuters reports. Chinese authorities report 16 deaths, 76 injured (up from 65 earlier reported) and 413 aftershocks. These figures are preliminary and may change.

The earthquake struck 191 km east-northeast of Nagqu at 22:33 local time (14:33 UTC), at a depth of 18 km, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). Magnitude is the USGS value (Mww); other agencies may publish different values. The humanitarian figures are reported by authorities, not USGS or PAGER estimates.

Earlier coverage: https://youtu.be/4ZrrJfRGJRQ (first report), https://youtu.be/d2v2iFsGi7w (16 dead, 339 homes collapsed)

Sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/china/injuries-chinas-tibet-rise-65-after-earthquake-death-toll-remains-16-2026-10-23/
- USGS: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us6000u43g
